subjects.label: Filming and extracting the footage
subjects.description: The camera as the job: pointing it at monsters and friends, running out of film, dying with the footage, and the extraction or upload step failing or losing the best video; stutter while recording with outside software belongs in performance.

subjects.label: Playing a YouTuber for views
subjects.description: The premise of being a content creator on SpookTube: chasing views, view addiction, the view quota and what it pays, subscribe-and-like jokes, demonetisation and copyright strikes; the horror mood and the co-op itself do not belong here.

subjects.label: Real creators and shows it recalls
subjects.description: Naming a real YouTuber, streamer, TV channel or programme the game feels like, from Mr Beast and Logan Paul to Dima Maslennikov, RTL Klub and Mir Naiznanku; comparisons to other games belong in genre.

subjects.label: Trolling and sacrificing friends for the camera
subjects.description: Co-op as a comedy generator: trapping a friend with a monster, selling out teammates, filming each other's backsides and the funny footage that comes out of it; plain praise for playing with friends or lobby trouble belongs in multiplayer.

subjects.label: Monsters and creatures
subjects.description: The creatures themselves: named or described monsters such as the feet licker, the snails, the ghosts' dad and the rocket dogs, how they behave, how aggressive they are and how many there are; the general fright they cause belongs in atmosphere.

subjects.label: Number and variety of maps
subjects.description: How many maps or environments there are, the same three coming round, how much a map changes between runs, and wishes for new settings such as Japanese forests; general length and replay value belong in content.

subjects.label: Lethal Company comparison
subjects.description: Measuring the game against Lethal Company, as a Lethal-like, a better or worse one, or Lethal Company with a twist; comparisons to anything else belong in genre.
